atoms.text: This guide configures FlowGate, a load balancer service, to deliver access logs to the bucket lb-access-logs-prod. FlowGate writes one gzip-compressed file every five minutes under the prefix flowgate/, using the key format flowgate/YYYY/MM/DD/<load-balancer-id>_<timestamp>.log.gz. Access is granted only through an IAM role named FlowGateLogDelivery, which FlowGate assumes each time it delivers a file. Create the role with a trust policy that allows the service principal flowgate.example.com to perform the assume-role action. Attach an identity-based policy to the role that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod/flowgate/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod. Leave the bucket policy unchanged, because it needs no statement that names FlowGate. When you enable access logging in the FlowGate console, enter the role ARN, the bucket name, and the prefix flowgate/. The first log file should appear within ten minutes; if it does not, check the role's trust policy and the resource ARN in the identity-based policy.

This guide configures FlowGate, a load balancer service, to deliver access logs to the bucket lb-access-logs-prod. FlowGate writes one gzip-compressed file every five minutes under the prefix flowgate/, using the key format flowgate/YYYY/MM/DD/<load-balancer-id>_<timestamp>.log.gz. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the FlowGate service principal directly. Add a statement to the bucket policy whose Principal is the service principal flowgate.example.com. The statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod/flowgate/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on arn:example:storage:::lb-access-logs-prod. Do not create an IAM role, because FlowGate delivers files as its service principal and no role ARN is required. When you enable access logging in the FlowGate console, enter the bucket name and the prefix flowgate/. The first log file should appear within ten minutes; if it does not, check the Principal value and the resource ARN in the bucket policy statement.

This guide sets up TrailKeeper, an audit logging service, to write account activity records to the bucket org-audit-archive. TrailKeeper delivers a JSON log file roughly every fifteen minutes under the prefix trails/<account-id>/, one directory per member account. Access is granted only through an IAM role named TrailKeeperDelivery, which TrailKeeper assumes for each delivery. The role's trust policy names the service principal trailkeeper.example.com as the entity allowed to assume it. Its identity-based policy allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::org-audit-archive/trails/* and storage:GetBucketAcl on the bucket itself. The bucket policy is not changed, so no existing statements need review. In the TrailKeeper console, create a trail, select the bucket, and supply the role ARN. After saving, confirm that a file appears under trails/ within thirty minutes, and review the role's policy if delivery status shows an access error.

This guide sets up TrailKeeper, an audit logging service, to write account activity records to the bucket org-audit-archive. TrailKeeper delivers a JSON log file roughly every fifteen minutes under the prefix trails/<account-id>/, one directory per member account. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, with no IAM role involved. The policy contains a statement whose Principal is the service principal trailkeeper.example.com. That statement allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::org-audit-archive/trails/* and storage:GetBucketAcl on the bucket itself. No role is created, so no trust policy or role ARN has to be maintained. In the TrailKeeper console, create a trail and select the bucket, with no role field to fill in. After saving, confirm that a file appears under trails/ within thirty minutes, and review the bucket policy statement if delivery status shows an access error.

This guide allows Edgeline, a content delivery service, to deliver request logs to the bucket cdn-request-logs. Edgeline writes a new log file for each edge location every hour, using keys of the form edgeline/<distribution-id>/<date>-<hour>-<edge-id>.gz. Access is granted only through an IAM role called EdgelineLogWriter that the Edgeline service assumes when it starts a delivery. Create the role and set its trust policy to permit the service principal edgeline.example.com to assume it. Give the role an identity-based policy with a single statement allowing storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::cdn-request-logs/edgeline/*. Make no changes to the bucket policy. In the Edgeline distribution settings, enable logging, choose the bucket, set the prefix edgeline/, and enter the role ARN. Logs for the first full hour should appear after about sixty minutes; a missing file usually means the role's resource ARN does not match the prefix.

This guide allows Edgeline, a content delivery service, to deliver request logs to the bucket cdn-request-logs. Edgeline writes a new log file for each edge location every hour, using keys of the form edgeline/<distribution-id>/<date>-<hour>-<edge-id>.gz. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the Edgeline service principal as the grantee. Add a bucket policy statement whose Principal is the service principal edgeline.example.com. Give that statement a single action, storage:PutObject, on arn:example:storage:::cdn-request-logs/edgeline/*. Do not create any IAM role for this purpose. In the Edgeline distribution settings, enable logging, choose the bucket, and set the prefix edgeline/. Logs for the first full hour should appear after about sixty minutes; a missing file usually means the bucket policy's resource ARN does not match the prefix.

This guide configures NameWatch, a DNS resolver service, to export query logs to the bucket dns-query-logs. NameWatch buffers queries and writes a newline-delimited JSON object every ten minutes to the prefix namewatch/<resolver-id>/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named NameWatchExporter, which NameWatch assumes at the start of each export. The role's trust policy lists the service principal namewatch.example.com. Its identity-based policy allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs/namewatch/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket, restricted to that prefix. The bucket policy remains as it was, with no new statements. In the NameWatch resolver configuration, turn on query logging and enter the bucket name, the prefix, and the role ARN. Run a test query and wait for the next ten-minute window; if no object appears, check that the role ARN was entered correctly and that its policy covers the prefix.

This guide configures NameWatch, a DNS resolver service, to export query logs to the bucket dns-query-logs. NameWatch buffers queries and writes a newline-delimited JSON object every ten minutes to the prefix namewatch/<resolver-id>/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the NameWatch service principal. Add a statement with the Principal namewatch.example.com that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::dns-query-logs/namewatch/* and storage:ListBucket on the bucket, restricted to that prefix. No IAM role is created, and the bucket policy is the only place the permissions are defined. In the NameWatch resolver configuration, turn on query logging and enter the bucket name and the prefix. Run a test query and wait for the next ten-minute window; if no object appears, check that the statement's Principal is correct and that its resources cover the prefix.

This guide covers cross-account delivery of PacketTrace network flow logs into the bucket netflow-central, which belongs to account 111122223333. PacketTrace runs in account 444455556666 and writes a compressed text file every five minutes under packettrace/444455556666/<region>/. Access is granted only through an IAM role named PacketTraceDelivery, created in account 111122223333, which the PacketTrace service assumes. The role's trust policy names the service principal packettrace.example.com and requires the source account value 444455556666. Its identity-based policy allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::netflow-central/packettrace/444455556666/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. The bucket policy is not edited. In account 444455556666, create a flow log subscription that points to the bucket and specifies the role ARN. Verify delivery by listing the prefix after ten minutes, and check the source-account condition in the trust policy if nothing arrives.

This guide covers cross-account delivery of PacketTrace network flow logs into the bucket netflow-central, which belongs to account 111122223333. PacketTrace runs in account 444455556666 and writes a compressed text file every five minutes under packettrace/444455556666/<region>/. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy in account 111122223333, which names the PacketTrace service principal. The statement's Principal is packettrace.example.com, with a condition requiring the source account value 444455556666. It allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::netflow-central/packettrace/444455556666/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. No IAM role is created in either account. In account 444455556666, create a flow log subscription that points to the bucket, without specifying a role. Verify delivery by listing the prefix after ten minutes, and check the source-account condition in the bucket policy if nothing arrives.

This guide enables QueryLens, a managed database service, to export slow query logs to the bucket db-slowlog-export. QueryLens uploads one text file per database instance each day at 00:30 UTC, using keys of the form querylens/<instance-name>/<date>.log. Access is granted only through an IAM role named QueryLensExport, which the database service assumes when the export job runs. The role's trust policy allows the service principal querylens.example.com to assume it. Attach an identity-based policy that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::db-slowlog-export/querylens/* and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on the same path, since large files are uploaded in parts. The bucket policy is left unchanged. In the instance's log export settings, select slow query logs, enter the bucket name, and provide the role ARN. After the next 00:30 UTC run, confirm the file exists, and if the job reports an authorization failure, review the actions listed in the role policy.

Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the QueryLens service principal. Add a statement with the Principal querylens.example.com that allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::db-slowlog-export/querylens/* and storage:AbortMultipartUpload on the same path, since large files are uploaded in parts. No IAM role is created for the export. In the instance's log export settings, select slow query logs and enter the bucket name, leaving out any role setting. After the next 00:30 UTC run, confirm the file exists, and if the job reports an authorization failure, review the actions listed in the bucket policy statement.

This guide configures GatewayLog, an API gateway service, to deliver structured access logs to the bucket api-access-logs. GatewayLog writes JSON Lines files to the prefix gatewaylog/<stage>/<date>/, creating a new file whenever the buffer reaches 50 MB or five minutes elapse. Access is granted only through an IAM role named GatewayLogWriter, assumed by the service for every file it writes. The trust policy of that role names the service principal gatewaylog.example.com. The role's identity-based policy allows storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::api-access-logs/gatewaylog/* and nothing else. The bucket policy is not modified. In the gateway stage settings, enable access logging, select the bucket, and enter the role ARN. Send a few test requests, then check the prefix after five minutes; if the stage reports a delivery error, compare the role's resource ARN with the configured prefix.

Send a few test requests, then check the prefix after five minutes; if the stage reports a delivery error, compare the bucket policy's resource ARN with the configured prefix.

This guide sets up PodSpool, a container orchestration service, to ship cluster logs to the bucket cluster-logs-archive. PodSpool writes one compressed file per namespace every hour under podspool/<cluster-name>/<namespace>/<date>/. When it starts, PodSpool also writes a small marker object named podspool/<cluster-name>/.delivery-check to confirm that writes succeed. Access is granted only through an IAM role named PodSpoolShipper, which the service assumes for all writes. The role's trust policy allows the service principal podspool.example.com to assume it. The identity-based policy permits storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::cluster-logs-archive/podspool/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. The bucket policy stays unchanged. In the cluster logging configuration, specify the bucket, the prefix podspool/, and the role ARN. Confirm that the marker object appears immediately; if it is absent, inspect the role's trust policy and identity-based policy.

This guide sets up PodSpool, a container orchestration service, to ship cluster logs to the bucket cluster-logs-archive. PodSpool writes one compressed file per namespace every hour under podspool/<cluster-name>/<namespace>/<date>/. When it starts, PodSpool also writes a small marker object named podspool/<cluster-name>/.delivery-check to confirm that writes succeed. Access is granted only through the bucket's resource-based policy, which names the PodSpool service principal for all writes. The statement's Principal is podspool.example.com. It permits storage:PutObject on arn:example:storage:::cluster-logs-archive/podspool/* and storage:GetBucketLocation on the bucket. No IAM role is created, so no trust policy exists. In the cluster logging configuration, specify the bucket and the prefix podspool/. Confirm that the marker object appears immediately; if it is absent, inspect the Principal and resource entries in the bucket policy statement.
